requirement.summary: TMS 2.0 - Incorrect change log info after change arrival cover
requirement.description:
Summary

TMS Operation: Change Arrival Cover writes the wrong reservation change log (Table# to [Empty] instead of Arrival Cover from/to).

Steps to Reproduce

- Open TMS Operation.

- Find a reservation that already has a table assigned (e.g. Table 5).

- Mark Host Arrived and set Arrival Cover (e.g. 2). Confirm the reservation is in Host Arrived status.

- Click Arrival again on the same reservation to open Change Arrival Cover.

- Change Arrival Cover from 2 to 4 and click Confirm.

- Open that reservation’s Change Log.

Expected Result

- Arrival Cover is updated successfully.

- Change log records the cover change, e.g. Arrival Cover : from 2 to 4.

- Table number is not logged as changed.

Actual Result

- Arrival Cover is updated, but change log is wrong: Table# : from 5 to [Empty].

- Arrival Cover from/to is not written.

- Cause: updateResvField (field=arrivalGuests) reloads the reservation with tables, then setResvLog compares old tables against empty saveData['TmsResvTable'], so it treats tables as unassigned. resv_arrival_guests was not in $checkResvFields, so Arrival Cover was never logged. The original cover was also overwritten before log write, so even if it were logged, from/to would be the same.

requirement.summary: TMS 2.0 - Incorrect table number arrived after mark arrival
requirement.description:
Email: ASE Report | SW | Shiji Cloud | KSL | KSL / Abnormal in TMS (Shang Palace) (HK Case #3345889)

Information:

It is found that sometimes mark arrival is using the old table but not the table changed.

Step to Reproduce:

- Open two browsers, and one open mark arrival for the reservation and hold the dialog

- Another tab change table for the reservation (either by edit booking or quick change)

- After table changed, back to the first tab to mark arrival

Expected Result:

The reservation will mark arrival with the changed table

Actual result:

The reservation will mark arrival with the table before change

Solution:

Add checking before mark arrival, if the mark arrival mismatch that with the table in the reservation record, return error and close the mark arrival dialog

requirement.summary: TMS 2.0 - POS getMembersByConditions fails on SQL Server (GROUP BY memb_id with SELECT *)
requirement.description:
What:

POS / TMS API getMembersByConditions (get_members_by_conditions) throws on SQL Server when the search joins membership (membership no / group no / interface code).

Cake find('all') selects MemMember.* (and belongsTo columns) but GROUP BY is only MemMember.memb_id. SQL Server requires every selected column to be grouped or aggregated (Msg 8120). ORDER BY membership number has the same problem.

MySQL usually passes because ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY is off. Strict MySQL would fail the same way.

GROUP BY is still required: one member can match multiple membership rows, which would duplicate paging rows without it.

Fix:

MemberApiGeneralComponent::getMembersByConditions — page distinct memb_id first (fields + GROUP BY memb_id + recursive -1, ORDER BY MIN(...) for non-id sort columns), then load full guest profiles with memb_id IN (...). POS payload unchanged. Count stays COUNT(DISTINCT memb_id).

After fix:

SQL Server and MySQL both return the same paged member list / full profile as before. Membership-no sort is deterministic (MIN(mmsh_member)) when one member matches multiple memberships.
requirement.release_notes:
Bug Fixing: [Jira-68259] TMS 2.0 - POS getMembersByConditions fails on SQL Server (GROUP BY memb_id with SELECT *)
Descriptions:
When POS / TMS calls get_members_by_conditions (members_by_conditions) and the search joins membership (membership_no / membership_group_no / interface_code), SQL Server throws Msg 8120 because the query SELECT * with GROUP BY memb_id only.
MySQL usually passes when ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY is off; strict MySQL would fail the same way.
After fix: page distinct memb_id first, then load full guest profiles. POS / TMS response payload is unchanged. SQL Server and MySQL both return the same paged member list.
Setup:
1. Use a SQL Server (repro target; MySQL can also be used for regression)
2. Prepare at least 1 active member with membership record(s) (membership no / group no as needed)
3. Optional: same member with >1 membership rows to verify paging is not duplicated
4. No new admin config. Existing Member + Membership data is enough
Step / Testing scope:
Call TMS REST API members_by_conditions via Postman (or POS search that uses this API) with membership join conditions.
Confirm HTTP 200, members[] + paging returned, no SQL Msg 8120.
Compare same search on MySQL if available - result set / paging should match.
Endpoint example:
GET {base}/rest_api/tms/members_by_conditions?is_json_response=true&membership_no={membershipNo}&page=1&limit=10
Expected result:
- Before: SQL Server error Msg 8120 (Column is invalid in the select list because it is not contained in either an aggregate function or the GROUP BY clause)
- After: normal reply with members[] and paging { page, current_page_record_count, total_record_count, page_count }
- Response field contract unchanged vs pre-fix (no new / removed POS fields)

requirement.summary: TMS 2.0 - MySQL table lock race: two users can lock / assign the same table (lock API + update resv field)
requirement.description:
Summary

On MySQL, two users can lock / assign the same table at the same time (same outlet, date, period).

This is not caused by HERO-67685. Both paths below use the same MySQL table-state write (updateTableState): check then insert, with no exclusive lock. MSSQL already uses sp_getapplock and is out of scope.

HERO-67685 moved Quick Edit Table to server lock on save, so this race on change table is more visible.

Affected paths

- *Lock table API* — floor plan lock / POST table_states (updateTableStates, action lock/block)

- *Update reservation field* — change table via updateResvField → __lockAndUnlockTable

Customer / Environment

- MySQL / Cloud TMS (e.g. Kowloon Shangri-La – Café Kool)

- MSSQL: no change

Steps to Reproduce

- MySQL TMS outlet, two users, same outlet / date / period.

- Path A: both lock the same vacant table at the same time (floor plan or lock table API).

- Path B: two reservations; both change table to the same table at the same time (update_fields).

Current Result

- Both requests can succeed.

- Two lock records can exist for the same table.

- Lock table API: both users can think they hold the lock.

- Update resv field: both reservations can be saved on the same table.

Expected Result

- Second request fails with the existing locked/blocked error.

- Only one lock record for that table.

Proposed Fix

MySQL GET_LOCK only, in TmsTableState::updateTableState (one place → both paths).

- GET_LOCK on outlet + period + date + table + ext (name ≤ 64 chars; timeout 30s, same as MSSQL).

- Success only if return value is 1.

- Under the lock: if table already locked/blocked, fail; else insert. Do not insert a second row.

- Always RELEASE_LOCK in finally (GET_LOCK is not released by commit).

- MSSQL path unchanged.

Do not add UNIQUE index or occupancy check in this ticket.

Acceptance Criteria

- Two concurrent lock table API calls on the same table: one success, one locked/blocked error; one lock row only.

- Two concurrent change-table saves (updateResvField) to the same table: one success, one conflict error.

- MSSQL behaviour unchanged.

Test plan (JMeter)

QA must test concurrency with JMeter, not only two browsers.

Scenarios

- Lock table API — N threads (e.g. 2 / 10 / 20) POST table_states action lock, same outlet / date / period / table, same second (no ramp-up).

- Update resv field — N threads update_fields change table to the same target table on different reservations (or same race as production).

- Repeat for different tables in parallel (no cross-table blocking).

Must pass

- Only *one* winner per table; others return locked/blocked (or existing conflict error). Not two success.

- tms_table_states: *one* lock row for that table key after the burst.

- *No deadlock* (MySQL SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS / error log: no deadlock; API must not hang until PHP timeout).

- *No GET_LOCK / InnoDB lock held > 30s* and left in DB:

- After the test, GET_LOCK is released (check performance_schema.metadata_locks / IS_USED_LOCK(name) = 0 / SHOW PROCESSLIST no waiting on named lock).

- GET_LOCK timeout is 30s: waiter either gets the lock within 30s or fails; must not wait forever.

- No leftover tms_table_states lock rows from a request that failed / timed out (failed acquire must not insert; failed request must still RELEASE_LOCK).

- InnoDB row locks from the insert must not remain after the request ends (no trx open > 30s on tms_table_states).

JMeter notes

- Use two (or more) login sessions / tokens.

- Ramp-up 0 for the race; then a soak (e.g. 1–2 min) to catch leaked locks.

- Capture response codes/error keys and a DB snapshot of tms_table_states + IS_USED_LOCK before/after.

Out of Scope

- UNIQUE index / duplicate-row cleanup

- Extra occupancy validation on standard TMS

- HERO-67685 FE lock storm

requirement.summary: Fixing undefined array key issues on PHP 8 (Owner Box Waitlist user + period oper_id)
requirement.description:
Summary

Two PHP 8 Undefined array key failures from the same pattern: copy a field that may not exist on the source array.

Case 1 — testGetOwnerBoxWaitlistReservations

- Symptom: Undefined array key "UserUser"

- Location: Plugin/Hkjc/Controller/Component/HkjcApiReservationComponent.php — getOwnerBoxWaitlistReservations

- Root Cause: Race schedule has rasc_waitlist_status_modify_by_user_id, so the code calls UserUser->findActiveById() and then uses $userUser['UserUser'][...] after only checking $userUser != ''. When findActiveById does not return the expected Cake structure (no UserUser key), PHP 8 raises Undefined array key "UserUser".

- Expected: If the modifier user cannot be loaded, name fields stay empty string. API still returns waitlist data. No PHP warning/error.

Case 2 — testGetPeriodOptions / testGetTableStatistics

Symptom: Undefined array key "oper_id" (same path can also miss oday_id)

Location: Plugin/Tms/Model/Behavior/TmsPeriodBehavior.php — buildPeriodArrayForSpecialMode (foreach over $periodInfoKeys copying $tmsPeriod[$periodInfoKey]). Called from TmsResvDateBehavior::loadPeriodsForSpecialMode.

Root Cause:

Both tests go through loadPeriodsForSpecialMode. For TmsOperatingPeriod, the behavior always copies oper_id / oday_id off the period row. That row does not always have oper_id (non-operating / deployed path). PHP 8 then fails on the copy loop.

Expected:

Period options / table statistics still return. Missing oper_id / oday_id is treated as empty/default. No PHP warning/error.
